review.scope: Follow-up hosted campaign prototype at current commit. Verify R1 JSON/Markdown blocker fixed through validated P001 artifact contract before admission, nonstring and reviewer-stage checks, original turn/packet/duplicate provenance, named socket refusals and preserved one-round cap. No installation, credential grant, patient or live activation. Review source only; report any remaining integration blockers.
findings: VERIFIED R1 BLOCKER FIX (protected_handover.model_output_format + model_stage): a strict campaign_artifacts contract (exactly {version,experiment,mode}; version type-strict int 1 excluding bools; experiment 'P001'; mode readiness|discuss; named CAMPAIGN_ARTIFACT_CONTRACT / CAMPAIGN_ARTIFACT_STAGE refusals) selects output_format='json' for continuation/review, so model_call now prepends 'Return one JSON object only', consistent with the adapter's one-JSON-object artifact instruction. model_stage computes the format after body-schema validation but before turn-folder creation, budget counting and admit_server, so a malformed contract fails closed before any admission or supervised turn budget is consumed. Legacy packets without campaign_artifacts retain markdown and the execution_proposal-disposition JSON path (asserted by test_campaign_json_format_is_explicit_and_legacy_unchanged). Source-only review; tests were not run.

VERIFIED PROVENANCE (hosted_campaign.BrokerStages): the <stage>.hosted-provenance.json record now binds the event (turn_id/attempt/source), packet_sha256 over the encoded packet, and broker_duplicate captured per stage from the broker response, alongside model_receipt_sha256/operating_context_sha256 with original_protocol_private true. Replayed completions are distinguishable from fresh calls, and the broker's binding.json check refuses a replay under a changed packet (TURN_BINDING_CHANGED), so the recovery adapter can bind artifacts to the exact protected turn without exposing private protocols.

VERIFIED NONSTRING AND REVIEWER-STAGE CHECKS: HOSTED_CAMPAIGN_FILE_SCHEMA now refuses non-dict answers, wrong key sets and any non-string value before any artifact write (test_nonstring_artifact_has_named_refusal asserts an empty directory on refusal); the reviewer index requires names==['review.json'] and stage=='campaign_<mode>_review' bound to the mode captured at the author index (HOSTED_CAMPAIGN_ARTIFACT_SCOPE), closing the R1 unvalidated-stage minor.

VERIFIED NAMED SOCKET REFUSALS: request_broker raises the broker's reason only when it matches [A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{1,100} (e.g. SUPERVISED_MODEL_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED) and collapses anything else to BROKER_REFUSED_RECONCILE; exchange() already sanitizes arbitrary exception text to BROKER_FAILURE_PRESERVED, so campaign blocked.json can distinguish named operational refusals while no request data or private diagnostic text can leak.

VERIFIED ONE-ROUND CAP AND AUTHORITY BOUNDARIES: execute keeps keyword-only max_rounds default 2 with bool-excluding validation (CAMPAIGN_ROUND_BOUND); run_pipeline pins max_rounds=1, P001 and readiness/discuss and requires the exact packet contract (HOSTED_CAMPAIGN_PACKET_CONTRACT); a single-round REVISE preserves the round-1 proposal, negative review.json and blocked.json with no hidden repair round; the stage counter leaves the broker's third stage for disposition and a reused BrokerStages fails closed (HOSTED_CAMPAIGN_AUTHOR_REVIEW_BOUND). No credential, admission grant, scheduler, patient handler or live activation is added, and under SCOUT_CI the adapter's hardcoded ci:False/adapter provenance is still refused by the pipeline's runner-provenance check.

MINOR / VERIFY BEFORE INTEGRATION (fail-closed, carried from R1): BrokerStages.call and __call__ still invoke text(answer)/text(content) with public_export's default limit while the broker transport and immutable writer use an explicit limit=1500000; public_export.py was not supplied, so confirm the default cannot refuse a legitimately large admitted answer. Unlike the R1 blocker, the completion remains recoverable via the broker's duplicate stage_status path after a code fix, so this is a pre-integration verification item, not a blocker.

MINOR (fail-closed naming nits): json.loads of the de-fenced answer can raise a raw JSONDecodeError whose text execute sanitizes to failure_code PIPELINE_STAGE_FAILED instead of a named HOSTED_CAMPAIGN_* code; and run_pipeline's dict-equality packet check would accept version=True (bool == 1), which the broker's type-strict contract then refuses at the first stage before admission. Both refuse safely; naming the parse failure and mirroring the broker's type-strict version check would keep failure codes exact.
